Attachments: runbook_v3.pdf (application/pdf), smoke-checklist.csv (text/csv)

Team + EdgeCorp,

Per our CAB approval this morning, we intend to run a full "cabinet switchplay" rehearsal on Friday to validate the on‑prem cutover sequence for the new VPC appliance racks. This is a dry run (no DNS changes) but will exercise the same procedural steps and interfaces we will use during the live cutover.

Quick agenda (60–90m):
- 09:30 — Bridge & roll call (Ops bridge)
- 09:35 — Preflight: power, console access, serial handoff
- 09:45 — Network sequence: TOR fabric check, BGP neighbor bringup, VLAN stitching
- 10:05 — KV cache priming + model shard health
- 10:20 — ACL sync + connectivity smoke (east→west path)
- 10:40 — Failure injection: link flap on mgmt plane (simulated)
- 10:55 — Walkthrough of incident playbook & rollback triggers

Please review the attached runbook_v3.pdf and the smoke-checklist.csv. Callouts: step 6 has the BGP neighbor timing and step 9 lists the exact ACL rules we sample.

ASKS: 
- Tom / EdgeCorp: confirm on‑site console badge list and the engineer who will perform console hands (we need serial access to rack 12B).
- Laura: can you confirm the expected BGP neighbor ASNs we should use for the rehearsal (we will mirror production numbers but put a simulated ASN in the BGP config)?
- All: confirm you can join the 09:30 bridge and the read/write access to the Drive link below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-runbooks

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin

Subject: Re: On‑prem cutover: cabinet switchplay smoke rehearsal

Marcus — thanks for the plan, looks good. Two quick adjustments from my side after scanning the runbook: 

1) BGP sequencing: insert an explicit "neighbor shutdown/unshutdown" backstop at step 6.5. If the neighbor flaps more than twice in 30s, abort to rollback posture A.
2) Add a preflight MTU verification on the TORs — we've tripped jumbo MTU mismatches in a lab before and it created asymmetric routes.

Connor — please bring the spare NICs (2x SFP+), we'll need them if a link doesn't come up cleanly.

I also left an inline comment on the Drive copy about the exact rule ID we'd sample in ACL sync — use rule 142 for verification, not 140 (typo in v3).

On quoting Marcus below for context:
> Please review the attached runbook_v3.pdf and the smoke-checklist.csv. Callouts: step 6 has the BGP neighbor timing and step 9 lists the exact ACL rules we sample.

I'll be on the bridge. Laura

Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: On‑prem cutover: cabinet switchplay smoke rehearsal — post rehearsal summary
Attachments: smoke-results.log (text/plain)

Quick readout from today's rehearsal — excellent collaboration, thanks all. Below are the results for the items in smoke-checklist.csv (sampling highlights only):

- Bridge & access — PASS. All required attendees on bridge; EdgeCorp whitelisted bridge IP at T‑15m.
- Preflight power & serial — PASS. Rack consoles reachable; serial access validated on 12B.
- BGP neighbor (simulated ASN 65099) — PASS. Neighbor established within expected timers (3s hold down).
- KV cache priming — PASS. Model shards responded and served warm tokens to test TTL window.
- ACL sync — PARTIAL FAIL → RETEST. Rule mismatch found (ACL rule 142 on TOR‑east showed old deny entry). Connor pushed corrected ACL and we rechecked: rule 142 now matching expected allow; post‑fix verification PASS.
- Failure injection (mgmt link flap) — PASS (no regression). Failover path triggered and control plane recovered in 22s.

Action items: 
- Connor: add a comment in the runbook to call out ACL rule ID verification explicitly (I put a TODO at step 9).
- Marissa: push the post‑rehearsal smoke-results.log to the engagement folder and update the runbook change log.
- Marcus: update incident playbook with the observed timing (control plane recovery = 22s) and convert the rehearsal notes to the CAB addendum.

Related artifacts: smoke-results.log (attached), runbook_v3.pdf (Drive link), CAB signed doc in thread.

Conclusion: rehearsal successful; the remaining minor risk (ACL sync) was remediated during the run and will be validated again during the live cutover. Recommend greenlight to proceed to scheduled cutover window next week, pending final signoff from EdgeCorp ops sponsor.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
